answer: Agents stake a token on a ledger, building a trellis of credit that must be rebonded each epoch; the ember‑light consensus timestamps bonds, so a new identity appears as a fresh branch on the karst‑like trust graph. A random jury of agents audits a sample of bonded nodes, and any discrepancy triggers a spot‑check penalty that burns the stake. Thus an attacker must buy and continually rebond tokens for every fake node, paying a linear cost equal to the number of identities he tries to sustain.
